study: External open-weights judges vs the in-house QAG judge
status: PARTIAL — one of four adapters reachable
question: Do published open-weights specialist judges already address the in-house judge thesis?
decision_rule: From run_external_judges_benchmark.py: re-evaluate the distillation thesis if any external judge lands within 3 F1 points of the >=0.75 projected landing zone, i.e. F1 >= 0.72.

at_best_swept_cut.scope: development fit on this same sample; no held-out estimate

judges_not_run.patronus-lynx-large: PATRONUS_API_KEY not available in this environment
judges_not_run.prometheus-2-7b: TOGETHER_API_KEY not available in this environment
judges_not_run.vectara-hhem-v2.1 (hosted): VECTARA_API_KEY not available; the open-weights arm above was run instead

in_house_comparator.caveat: The repository marks this table as predating 0.17.0's stricter verdict parser and states it needs revalidation. It is not a current measurement.

verdict: No pivot indicated on point estimate. HHEM-2.1-open reaches F1 0.644 at its vendor default cut and 0.674 at the best swept cut, both below the 0.72 trigger.
The run does not exclude the trigger either: the bootstrap intervals reach 0.750 and 0.777, so n=100 cannot rule out a judge at or above 0.72.
The comparison is additionally weak because the in-house comparator is a stale number the repository itself flags for revalidation.
Cheapest way to make this decision sound: rerun the in-house HaluEval QA arm under the current parser, then compare against this HHEM run on the same selection.
Scope: one dataset, one sample of 100 labelled pairs, one external judge. Two of the three hosted specialist judges remain unmeasured.
reproduce: benchmarks/run_external_judges_benchmark.py now carries a _vectara_hhem_local_score adapter that needs no API key (pip install torch 'transformers<5'). HHEM's custom model code does not load on transformers 5.x.
